scenarios.title: A Key Down the Side
text: Someone has dragged a key down the whole length of {CAR}, parked outside the training ground. The word scratched into the door is not a compliment.
{CAR} has been egged in the stadium car park after a defeat. Somebody has also written something on the windscreen in lipstick.

choices.label: Fix it quietly and say nothing
choices.text: He gets it fixed and says nothing. A fan forum finds out anyway and is mortified on the club's behalf.

choices.label: Post a photo with a joke
choices.text: 'At least they spelled it right.' The post goes viral. The vandal is found by other fans within a day and apologises publicly.

choices.label: Report it and push for charges
choices.hint: Fair. Some fans will think it's too much.
choices.text: The police find the culprit on camera: a sixteen-year-old. {J} drops the charges after meeting him. They take a photo together.

scenarios.title: The Crash
text: Wet road, a moment's distraction, a lamppost. He walks away with a bruised shoulder. {CAR} doesn't walk away at all.
A truck runs a red light and clips the back of {CAR}. Nobody is hurt. The car is a write-off. The photos of the wreck are online before the tow truck arrives.

choices.label: Thank the heavens and get checked out
choices.text: The scans are clear. {MUM} makes him promise to drive like a grandmother. The car is gone.

out.text: He plays and scores. 'Indestructible,' say the papers. The shoulder hurts for a month.
The shoulder seizes up in the warm-up. A minor injury, a major lesson.

scenarios.title: Flashed
scenarios.text: Caught on camera doing 160 in an 80 zone in {CAR}, on the way to training because he was late. The photo, with his face clearly visible, has been leaked to a newspaper.

choices.label: Apologise publicly and pay the fine
choices.text: A short apology, a fine, a road-safety video for a children's charity. The story dies in two days.

choices.label: Hire a lawyer to fight it

out.text: The lawyer finds a technicality. He gets off. The headline: 'RICH FOOTBALLER ESCAPES SPEEDING BAN.'
The lawyer fails. Now it's a speeding story and an arrogance story.

choices.label: Get a driver
choices.text: He hires a driver and works on his phone in the back seat. He's never late again.

scenarios.title: The Watch
scenarios.text: A man on a motorbike rips the watch off his wrist at a red light and is gone before he can react. His wrist is bleeding. His heart is pounding.

choices.label: Report it and move on
choices.text: He reports it and decides it's a lesson. He was lucky the man didn't have a knife.

choices.label: Hire security
choices.text: He hires a security driver. It feels excessive until the next time someone follows him home.

choices.label: Stop wearing expensive things in public
choices.text: He leaves the expensive things in the safe. A cheap digital watch becomes his trademark.

scenarios.title: To the Moon
scenarios.text: {T} swears he's made a fortune on a new coin called SAMBACOIN. 'Get in now, before it goes to the moon.' He shows {J} a chart that only goes up.

out.text: It triples in a week. He sells. {T} doesn't. {T} loses everything a week later.
It goes to zero in nine days. The founders disappear. {T} can't look him in the eye.

choices.label: Put in a tiny amount, for fun
choices.hint: Lose a little, learn a lot.
choices.text: He puts in pocket money. It goes to zero. Cheap lesson.

choices.label: Say no
choices.text: He says no. A month later {T} is asking the squad for a loan.

scenarios.title: Who Looks After Your Money?
scenarios.text: His savings have grown faster than his knowledge of what to do with them. Three different 'advisers' have approached him this month. One drove a car worth more than his house.

choices.label: A boring, regulated firm
choices.text: A quiet woman in a cheap suit explains index funds, pensions and taxes. It's the most useful meeting of his life.

choices.label: The flashy one with the great returns
choices.desc: Twenty per cent a year, guaranteed.
choices.text: Twenty per cent a year, guaranteed. It works for a while. Then the emails stop.

choices.label: Learn to manage it yourself
choices.text: He reads three books on investing on the team bus. {T} calls him 'the Professor'.

scenarios.title: Gone
scenarios.text: The adviser's office is empty. His phone is disconnected. The 'fund' was never real. {J} has lost {loss}. He's not the only footballer: there are eleven others.

choices.label: Go to the police with the others
choices.text: Twelve footballers file a joint complaint. The adviser is arrested in another country eighteen months later. They get back a fraction.

choices.label: Go public as a warning
choices.desc: So it doesn't happen to young players.
choices.text: His interview about being scammed is used by the players' union in every academy. Young players stop him to say thank you.

scenarios.title: The Tax Office
scenarios.text: A letter from the tax authorities: an audit of his image rights and sponsor income for the last three years. His accountant goes very pale.

choices.label: Cooperate fully
choices.hint: If it's all clean, it's fine.

out.text: Six months of paperwork. Everything is in order, apart from a small mistake. A small fine. Over.
Mistakes were made, not by him, but in his name. The back taxes are big. Paying them hurts.

choices.label: Hire the most expensive tax lawyers
choices.text: The lawyers cost a fortune. The audit ends quietly. The bill for the lawyers does not.

scenarios.title: The Yacht Party
scenarios.text: His yacht is moored in the marina and everyone he has ever met wants to be invited aboard. A famous DJ has offered to play. A gossip photographer has already rented a boat nearby.
scenarios.prompt: Throw a party on your yacht?

out.text: The party is the talk of the summer. The photos are mostly harmless. Mostly.
A guest falls overboard. He's fine. The headlines are not.

choices.label: A quiet day with family
choices.text: {DAD} catches a fish and talks about it for a year. {MUM} gets seasick and laughs about it. Best day of the summer.

scenarios.title: The Yacht Bill
scenarios.text: The yacht's annual running costs have arrived: crew, mooring, fuel, insurance, a broken engine part flown in from Italy. The number is bigger than his first club's whole wage bill.

choices.label: Keep it
choices.text: He keeps it. Every time he steps on board, he remembers why.

choices.label: Charter it out when you're not using it
choices.text: Chartering covers half the costs. A famous rapper rents it for a week and leaves it spotless, surprisingly.

scenarios.title: Break-In
scenarios.text: Burglars broke into his house during an away match, while everyone knew where he was: on TV. They took jewellery, cash and the shirt from his debut. That last one hurts the most.
scenarios.prompt: Your home was burgled during a match.

choices.label: Upgrade security and move on
choices.text: Cameras, alarms, a guard at the gate. The house feels safe again, and a little like a prison.

choices.label: Appeal for the debut shirt
choices.text: His appeal for the shirt is shared a million times. A week later it's left in a bag at the stadium gate with an anonymous note: 'Sorry, we didn't know.'

scenarios.title: An Offer for Your Property
scenarios.text: A developer has made an unsolicited offer on one of his properties: well above what he paid. They want to build something enormous next door, and his place is in the way.

choices.label: Sell
choices.text: He sells. The profit is real. The tower they build next door is very ugly.

choices.label: Hold out for more
choices.desc: They need it more than you do.

out.text: The developer doubles the offer. He sells for a fortune.
The developer builds around him instead. His view is now a concrete wall.

choices.label: Keep it
choices.text: He keeps it. Money isn't everything. Sometimes.

scenarios.title: The Supercar and the Defeat
scenarios.text: He drives into training the day after a bad defeat in {CAR}. Someone films it. 'Glad someone's happy,' says the caption. Twenty thousand angry comments follow.
scenarios.prompt: Fans are angry about your car after a loss.

choices.label: Drive something modest for a while
choices.text: He turns up in his dad's old car for a month. Fans notice. The anger fades.

choices.label: It's my money
choices.text: 'I earned it.' True. The fans hear something else.

choices.label: Ignore it
choices.text: It passes, mostly. The supercar becomes a chant at away games.

scenarios.title: A Foundation
scenarios.text: His lawyer suggests a charitable foundation: tax-efficient, his name on something good, and a structure for all the requests he gets. {MUM} suggests something simpler: help the kids from his old neighbourhood.

choices.label: Start it, for kids from your old neighbourhood
choices.text: The {J} Foundation's first project is a pitch in his old neighbourhood. He's there on opening day, playing with forty kids in his socks.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.desc: You want to do it properly.
choices.text: He puts it off. It's a promise to himself he intends to keep.

scenarios.title: Where the Money Went
scenarios.text: A journalist reports that a manager at his foundation has been paying himself far too much and spending donations on a car. {J} had no idea. His name is on the door.

choices.label: Fire him, audit everything, publish the results
choices.text: Everything is published. He repays the donors from his own pocket. Donations go up the following year.

choices.label: Handle it quietly
choices.text: Handling it quietly looks like a cover-up. The second story is worse than the first.

scenarios.title: Thirty-Minute Flights
scenarios.text: A climate account has tracked his private jet: thirty-one flights this year, several shorter than an hour. The post is going viral alongside a photo of him wearing a 'save the planet' T-shirt at a charity event.
scenarios.prompt: You're being called a hypocrite over your jet.

choices.label: Sell the jet and say why
choices.text: He sells it and says, simply, that they had a point. The climate account thanks him. Some fans are surprised to find they like him more.

choices.label: Offset the emissions and keep it
choices.text: He funds a reforestation project. Half the internet applauds; half calls it greenwashing. The jet stays.

choices.label: Ignore it
choices.text: He ignores it. The account keeps tracking. Every flight becomes a post.

scenarios.title: Rich and Lonely
scenarios.text: Since the money came, his old friends have been strange: they won't let him pay, or they always let him pay, or they bring up his car in every conversation. {BFf} is the only one who still acts normal.

choices.label: Talk about it openly with the old crew
choices.text: One honest night in the old café. They admit they don't know how to act around him now. He admits he doesn't either. It gets better.

choices.label: Pay for everything, always
choices.text: He pays for everything. They let him. Something gets lost.

choices.label: Hang out mostly with other footballers
choices.text: His circle becomes footballers and their partners. Easier, smaller, a little hollow.

scenarios.title: Where Did It Go?
scenarios.text: His accountant sends a summary of last month's spending. Restaurants, clothes, a watch he doesn't remember buying, flights for friends, a 'gift' for someone whose name he can't place. The number has a lot of zeros.
scenarios.prompt: Your spending is out of control.

choices.label: Cut back hard
choices.text: He sets a budget and sticks to it, mostly. His accountant sends a smiley face for the first time ever.

choices.label: Earn more instead
choices.text: He signs up for every appearance going. The money comes in. So does the exhaustion.

choices.label: You only live once
choices.hint: Footballers who think this end up broke.
choices.text: It's fine, he tells himself. It's fine.

scenarios.title: The Restaurant
scenarios.text: A famous chef wants to open a restaurant with his name on it: '{J}'s Kitchen'. He needs {stake} and {J}'s face on the menu. The chef's last two restaurants closed.
scenarios.prompt: Invest in a restaurant with your name on it?

out.text: It's a hit. Matchday queues round the block. His mother refuses to eat there because her cooking is better.
It closes after fourteen months. The sign with his name on it ends up in a skip. Someone photographs it.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: He declines. The restaurant opens with a rival player's name on it instead.

scenarios.title: Prenup
scenarios.text: His lawyer, his agent and, awkwardly, {DAD} all say the same thing: before things get any more serious with {Pf}, he needs to think about a prenup.
scenarios.prompt: Raise the subject of a prenup?

choices.label: Talk to {Pf} about it honestly
choices.hint: Could go fine. Could go very badly.

out.text: {Pf} laughs: 'I was going to suggest one, I have savings too.' They sign it over dinner. It's oddly romantic.
{Pf} hears 'I don't trust you'. It takes a long time to undo.

choices.label: Don't mention it
choices.text: He never mentions it. His lawyer sighs and closes the file.

scenarios.title: What's It Worth?
scenarios.text: A shirt he wore in a famous match has appeared at an auction house, sold by a former teammate who swapped it with him years ago. The estimate is enormous.
scenarios.prompt: Your old shirt is being auctioned.

choices.label: Buy it back
choices.text: He bids anonymously and wins. The shirt goes in a frame. He finds out later it was the other bidder's dream shirt.

choices.label: Let it go
choices.text: It sells to a museum. He visits it once, incognito.

scenarios.title: A House for {MUM} and {DAD}
scenarios.text: {MUM} and {DAD} still live in the small rented house where he grew up. The roof leaks every rainy season. {DAD} pretends not to notice. {MUM} has a bucket for every leak.

choices.label: Build it
choices.text: A year later, he hands {MUM} the keys. She walks through every room twice and then sits on the kitchen floor and cries. {DAD} plants a mango tree in the garden.

choices.label: Fix the old house instead
choices.text: A new roof, a new kitchen, the same house. {MUM} says it's perfect. It is.

scenarios.title: The Long-Lost Brother
scenarios.text: A man claiming to be his father's son from another relationship has appeared with a lawyer and a story. {DAD} has gone very quiet.
scenarios.prompt: A stranger claims to be your half-brother.

choices.label: Ask for a DNA test, kindly

out.text: It's true. The man is his half-brother. {DAD} has some explaining to do. Slowly, they get to know each other.
It's false. The man disappears, and so does his lawyer.

choices.label: Talk to {DAD} first
choices.text: {DAD} tells him the truth, haltingly. It's complicated. The family will survive it, eventually.

scenarios.title: The Free Car
scenarios.text: A car brand sponsoring the club has 'gifted' every first-team player a new car, on condition they post about it and drive it to training. It's fine. It's beige.
scenarios.prompt: The club's car sponsor wants you driving their car.

choices.label: Drive it, post it, smile
choices.text: He drives the beige car with good grace. It's actually very comfortable. He'd never admit it.

choices.label: Give it to {DAD}
choices.text: {DAD} drives it everywhere with the club logo proudly on the side. The sponsor finds the story charming.

scenarios.title: Insure Your Legs?
scenarios.text: An insurance broker wants to insure his body: a big premium, but a huge payout if a career-ending injury happens. His agent says every serious player should have it.

choices.label: Yes
choices.text: He signs. The premium hurts every year. He hopes he never needs it.

choices.label: No
choices.text: He decides against it. He touches wood every time someone mentions it.

scenarios.title: The Thank-You Gift
scenarios.text: Tradition at the club: when a player hits a milestone, he buys the squad a gift. {J} has just reached a big one. The last player bought everyone a pair of trainers.
scenarios.prompt: What do you buy the squad?

choices.label: Something extravagant
choices.text: Twenty-five watches. The squad screams. The kit man cries. The next player to hit a milestone is very worried.

choices.label: Something personal
choices.desc: A framed photo of each player's best moment.
choices.text: Each player gets a framed photo of his best moment at the club. Several of them hang it at home.

choices.label: Dinner for everyone, families too
choices.text: A huge dinner with every player's family. The kids run riot. The best night of the season.

scenarios.title: The Empty House
scenarios.text: His house back home has been empty since he moved abroad. A cousin wants to live there 'to look after it'. An estate agent wants to rent it out properly.
scenarios.prompt: What happens to your empty house?

choices.label: Rent it out properly
choices.text: A nice family rents it. The rent pays for {MUM}'s monthly allowance.

choices.label: Let the cousin stay
choices.text: The cousin moves in. Then his girlfriend. Then her brothers. The house is full, the bills are unpaid.

scenarios.title: Fake Shirts
scenarios.text: His name is on thousands of fake shirts in every market in the country. They're cheap, they're terrible and kids love them. His agent wants to sue the factories.

choices.label: Sue the factories
choices.hint: Legally right. Kids lose their cheap shirts.
choices.text: The factories are shut down. Market stalls empty. Some fans say he's punishing poor kids.

choices.label: Launch a cheap official line
choices.text: An official shirt at market prices. It sells millions. The fakes disappear because nobody needs them.

choices.label: Leave it
choices.text: He shrugs. 'If a kid wants my name on his back, I won't stop him.' The quote is everywhere.

scenarios.title: The Foundation Gala
scenarios.text: His foundation's first gala: famous guests, an auction, a speech he has to give. The event planner wants a celebrity host. {MUM} wants to give the speech instead.
scenarios.prompt: Who speaks at your foundation's gala?

choices.label: Let {MUM} speak
choices.desc: She's the reason for all of it.
choices.text: {MUM} speaks for four minutes in her own language with subtitles behind her. There isn't a dry eye in the room. Donations triple.

choices.label: Give the speech yourself
choices.text: He talks about the pitch behind his school and the kids still playing there. The room stands.

scenarios.title: The Club Owner's Son
scenarios.text: The son of a billionaire wants to be friends. Private jets, private islands, private everything. Every weekend there's a new invitation. Every photo is a temptation.
scenarios.prompt: A billionaire's son wants you in his world.

choices.label: Accept the invitations
choices.text: Monaco one weekend, a yacht the next. The photos are stunning. His form is not.

choices.label: Accept once, then politely decline
choices.text: One weekend of absurd luxury. Then he goes back to his life. The billionaire's son respects it, oddly.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: He declines. The son finds another footballer to collect.

scenarios.title: Too Much
scenarios.text: He drives past the neighbourhood where he grew up and sees kids playing barefoot on the same dirt pitch he played on. He's wearing a watch that costs more than their parents earn in ten years.

choices.label: Fund a proper pitch for them
choices.text: Three months later there's a proper pitch with lights. He plays the opening match barefoot, out of respect.

choices.label: Give a percentage of everything, forever
choices.text: He pledges ten per cent of his income to youth football for the rest of his career. He tells nobody. {MUM} tells everybody.

choices.label: Accept that you earned it
choices.text: He reminds himself of the 5am runs and the bus rides. He earned it. The kids on the pitch stay on his mind anyway.

scenarios.title: BetKing
scenarios.text: A betting company called BetKing wants him as its face: an enormous fee for three adverts and a monthly post. His agent says the money is the biggest he'll ever see from a sponsor. {MUM} says gambling ruined her brother.

choices.label: Refuse
choices.text: He refuses and says why in an interview. A charity for gambling addiction asks him to be its patron.

choices.label: Take it
choices.text: The money is enormous. So is the backlash. {MUM} doesn't mention it, which is worse.

scenarios.title: The First Car
scenarios.text: He finds his first car, the battered old hatchback he bought with his first wage, for sale online. Rusty, sad, eleven owners later.

choices.label: Buy it and restore it
choices.text: He restores it lovingly. It sits in his garage next to cars worth fifty times more. It's the only one he talks about.

choices.label: Let it go
choices.text: He scrolls past. Some things are better as memories.

scenarios.title: The Partner
scenarios.text: His business partner has been running the business into the ground while telling him everything is fine. The accounts are a mess. There are debts he never knew about.
scenarios.prompt: Your business partner lied to you.

choices.label: Take control and fix it
choices.text: He fires the partner, hires a proper manager and puts in more money. The business survives, barely.

choices.label: Sell your stake and walk away
choices.text: He sells for a fraction of what he put in. Lesson expensive, lesson learned.

scenarios.title: A Gift From a Watchmaker
scenarios.text: A famous watchmaker sends him a limited-edition watch as a gift, with a note hoping he'll wear it at his next press conference. There's no contract. Just the watch.

choices.label: Wear it at the press conference
choices.text: He wears it. Watch forums identify it within an hour. The brand calls his agent the next day.

choices.label: Return it politely
choices.text: He sends it back with a kind note. The brand is impressed. They'll be back with a proper offer.

scenarios.title: Complaints
scenarios.text: His neighbours in the expensive gated community have complained: loud music, too many cars, his friends' motorbikes. The residents' committee wants a meeting.

choices.label: Apologise and invite them over
choices.text: He invites the whole street for a barbecue. The retired judge next door turns out to be a huge fan. Peace.

choices.label: Ignore them
choices.hint: A tabloid story waiting to happen.
choices.text: A neighbour sells the story to a tabloid: 'MY NIGHTMARE LIVING NEXT TO {J}'.
